Traditional Mexican Tamales for Dia de los Muertos

Served at: Dia de los Muertos

Makes about 12 tamalesPrep 45 minCook 1 hour

Tamales are a beloved traditional dish made of masa dough filled with various savory or sweet fillings, wrapped in corn husks, and steamed. They hold a special place during Dia de los Muertos celebrations, symbolizing offerings to honor deceased loved ones and bringing families together to share memories and food.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups masa harina (corn dough flour)
  • 2 1/2 cups chicken broth (or vegetable broth)
  • 1 1/2 cups lard or vegetable shortening
  • 2 teaspoons baking powder
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 2 cups cooked shredded chicken (or pork or vegetables for filling)
  • 1 cup red chile sauce (or green chile sauce, optional)
  • 24 dried corn husks, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

Method

  1. Soak the dried corn husks in warm water for at least 30 minutes until pliable.
  2. In a large bowl, beat the lard or shortening until fluffy.
  3. In a separate bowl, combine masa harina, baking powder, and salt.
  4. Gradually add the masa mixture to the lard, alternating with chicken broth, mixing well until a soft dough forms.
  5. Test the dough by dropping a small piece in cold water; if it floats, it’s ready. If not, beat in a little more lard.
  6. Drain the corn husks and pat dry.
  7. Spread about 2 tablespoons of masa dough onto the smooth side of each husk, leaving a border around the edges.
  8. Place 1-2 tablespoons of shredded chicken mixed with chile sauce in the center of the masa.
  9. Fold the sides of the husk toward the center, then fold the bottom up to enclose the filling.
  10. Arrange the tamales standing upright in a steamer basket with the open end up.
  11. Steam the tamales over boiling water for about 1 hour, checking occasionally to add more water as needed.
  12. Tamales are done when the masa easily pulls away from the husk.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian option, use sautéed vegetables and cheese as filling.
  • Use fresh homemade chile sauce for authentic flavor or store-bought for convenience.
  • Tamales can be made a day ahead and reheated by steaming or microwaving wrapped in a damp paper towel.
